title: English Vinglish Is Getting a Sequel. So Are Rangeela, Tere Naam, and Tanu Weds Manu. Bollywood Just Opened Its Vault.
excerpt: Eros Innovation has unveiled an ambitious slate that turns six beloved films into franchise properties, launches a nine-title mythology universe, and brings back Rajinikanth's Kochadaiiyaan in remastered glory.
body:
Something opened in Bollywood this week that had nothing to do with a box office. It was a vault.

Eros Innovation — the company behind some of Hindi cinema's most defining titles of the last three decades — has announced a sprawling content slate that reads less like a production calendar and more like a love letter to everyone who grew up on these films. At its centre is the Eros Universe initiative: six beloved films, each being expanded into franchise properties with new stories, new characters, and new formats.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=wGGmyaurjAI

The titles? Tanu Weds Manu. English Vinglish. Rangeela. Tere Naam. Desi Boyz. Phobia.

Pause on that lineup for a moment. These aren't just films — they're generational markers. English Vinglish was the late Sridevi's triumphant return, a quiet masterpiece that made every immigrant who ever stumbled through a new language feel seen. Rangeela was peak '90s Mumbai cinema — Urmila Matondkar at her magnetic best, A.R. Rahman's soundtrack on every Walkman, Aamir Khan in a role that felt like bottled charisma. Tere Naam is the film that proved Salman Khan could actually, genuinely act. And Tanu Weds Manu gave us Kangana Ranaut at her funniest and most unfiltered, opposite an R. Madhavan so endearing you wanted to protect him from his own marriage.

Now they're all coming back. But not quite the way you remember.

The first title with confirmed production details is Tanu Weds Manu: The Next Chapter, set to go on floors in 2026. Here's where it gets interesting: Mitakshara Kumar — best known for directing Heeramandi and The Empire — is taking over from franchise creator Aanand L. Rai. The film is co-produced with Rudrak Soma Jyoti Limited. While multiple reports suggest Kangana and Madhavan will reunite, the makers have also mentioned a new cast that will expand the universe. Whether that means new characters alongside Tanu and Manu or a full generational shift remains, for now, a delicious tease.

The English Vinglish expansion is arguably the most emotionally loaded announcement on the slate. Sridevi's 2012 masterpiece — written and directed by Gauri Shinde — was a film that existed in perfect, self-contained beauty. Any continuation will carry the weight of that legacy. No casting has been announced, and it's unclear whether the expansion will take the form of a direct sequel, a spin-off, or something across animation and microdramas. But the very fact that Eros is touching this property tells you they understand what it means — and what it will cost them if they get it wrong.

For the diaspora, these aren't just films you once watched. They're the films you showed your non-Indian friends to explain something about yourself. English Vinglish is still the film NRI parents recommend to their American-born children. Rangeela still plays at Indian film retrospectives from London to Toronto. Tanu Weds Manu gets quoted at every desi house party. Having these properties expanded — potentially across streaming, animation, and theatrical releases — means the cultural touchstones of one generation could become the shared mythology of the next.

"We are bringing together original mythology-inspired stories, beloved film titles, and classic cinema under one umbrella. Our aim is to create stories that can engage audiences across generations and formats." — Kishore Lulla, Founder and Chairman, Eros Innovation

But the slate doesn't stop at nostalgia. Eros has also unveiled Eros Brahmand — a mythology-based cinematic universe comprising nine original titles: Nandi: War of Kailasa, Dwaarka: Gateway to the Universe, Vimaan Wars, Mahabharat 5000 A.D., Yakshinis, Brahmarakshak, Garuda, Kumbhayanna, and Mansa Devi. If even half of these get made, it would represent the most ambitious mythology-to-screen project in Indian cinema history — Bollywood's answer to the interconnected universes that Hollywood has built from comic books.

And then there's the restoration play. Eros Remastered will kick off with Kochadaiiyaan — Rajinikanth's 2014 motion-capture epic that was India's first of its kind. Soundarya Rajinikanth, who directed the original, will oversee the restoration. The film was ahead of its time when it released — arguably too far ahead — and a remaster with 2026 technology could finally let audiences see what was always intended.

Whether Eros can execute at this scale is the billion-rupee question. Nine mythology films, six franchise expansions, and a remaster programme is a staggering amount of content for a company that hasn't been in the conversation for tentpole releases in years. But the fact that they're reaching for these specific titles, in this specific moment, tells you something about where Indian cinema thinks its audience lives: not just in multiplexes, but in memory.
